fieldMarks: Olive to pale grey-brown toad, 47-115 mm, with large dark green blotches edged in white covering the back.
Cranial ridges between the eyes diverge in a V and meet at the snout in a raised knob or shield (Woodhouse's toad has an L-shaped crest).
Faint pale stripe down the rear back; belly mostly white and rarely spotted.
Spades on the heels of the hind feet for digging.
behavior: Nocturnal and solitary; spends most of the year dormant in burrows 15-55 cm deep, emerging after heavy rain or at breeding.
Males call with a loud continuous trill of 20-50 seconds from shallow rain pools and flooded areas.
Sit-and-wait feeder on beetles, ants, moth larvae and other insects, mostly at night.
habitat: Short-grass prairie, desert, semidesert shrubland, open floodplains and irrigated farmland, typically in stream valleys, on heavier soils than Woodhouse's toad.
Breeds in temporary rain pools, flooded areas and fluctuating ponds.
range: Great Plains, southwestern US and northern Mexico: from southern Manitoba and southeastern Alberta south to central Mexico; east to western Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri and Oklahoma, west to central Montana, Colorado and southeastern California.

lookalikes.name: Woodhouse's toad
lookalikes.howToTell: Woodhouse's toad has an L-shaped cranial crest and a white back stripe rather than a raised snout shield with V-shaped ridges and large white-edged blotches.
